key_insight: TextSeal2 embeds detectable watermarks in LLM-generated text without changing the model’s output distribution. Its watermark survives speculative decoding—even when rejected draft tokens are replaced—without changing acceptance rates or adding measurable inference latency.
problem_solved: LLM watermarking must preserve output quality and diversity while remaining compatible with fast generation. Speculative decoding poses a particular challenge: replacement tokens must retain the watermark without disrupting draft-token acceptance.
method: Uses copula mixing and memoryless races to build a distortion-free watermark, as indicated by the paper’s title.
Keeps replacement tokens watermarked with the same keys after speculative drafts are rejected, while leaving acceptance rates unchanged.
Builds on TextSeal’s two-key, coin-flip approach to preserving diversity; the supplied abstract is truncated before explaining the full improvement.
impact: TextSeal2 could let practitioners add provenance signals to generated text without sacrificing output diversity or speculative-decoding speed. The abstract reports no measurable inference latency overhead.
visual_elements: Speculative-decoding flowchart showing accepted drafts and replacement tokens both retaining the watermark.
Side-by-side token-distribution illustration showing unchanged output probabilities with watermarking.
Two-key schematic contrasting TextSeal’s coin-flip routing with TextSeal2’s copula mixing.
Three metric badges: preserved diversity, unchanged acceptance rate, and no measurable added latency.
paper_title: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing and Memoryless Races
paper_authors: Tom Sander, Pierre Fernandez, Itai Gat, Haiming Bao, Jiaxin Shi
